name: Ignatius of Antioch
bio: Ignatius of Antioch, also called Theophorus, was bishop of the Church at Antioch in Syria in the late first and early second century. He is counted among the Apostolic Fathers, the earliest Christian writers after the New Testament.

Arrested and taken under guard from Syria to Rome, he wrote seven letters on the way: to the Churches of Ephesus, Magnesia, Tralles, Rome, Philadelphia and Smyrna, and to Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna. According to tradition he was martyred at Rome under the emperor Trajan, c. 108 AD. The letters are given here in Kirsopp Lake’s English version (Loeb Classical Library, The Apostolic Fathers, vol. I, 1912).
